note:
Hand-authored from Rewards Chest (Fortis Colosseum) revid 15285141 (re-fetched fresh this session; the only diff against the 2026-08-11 snapshot was a 'Smol heredit' -> 'Smol Heredit' capitalization fix, confirmed by diff) -- no Module:/Calculator: page exists for this source (checked directly: Category:Calculators has no Fortis Colosseum/Sol Heredit/Rewards Chest entry, and none of the three related pages transcludes or links one), so the wave-rate table the page publishes IS the complete source, not an approximation of a hidden formula. CORRECTED 2026-08-21 (see docs/DECISIONS.md's Fortis Colosseum accumulation-fix entry): each of the 12 waves is its OWN complete, self-contained weighted table exactly as published (rows verified to sum exactly to that wave's own denominator) -- but the earlier claim that this meant a NON-additive, exact-match selection (ctx.wavesReached via levelAtLeast n=atMost=W, picking only the final wave's table) was wrong. The page states plainly that the player 'walk[s] away with the rewards they've accumulated so far', i.e. loot is bankable and cumulative across every wave cleared, structurally identical to Doom of Mokhaiotl's already-correct 'every level up to the one reached fires its own roll' shape. Fixed to plain levelAtLeast('wavesReached', n) with no atMost, so ctx.wavesReached >= W activates wave W's table for every W it has passed, not just the final one. Sanity check: summing the wiki's own published per-wave 'overall unique chance' figures for waves 4-12 gives an overall unique chance of ~22% for a full wave-12 clear, matching widely-reported community figures (~20-25%) for a full Colosseum clear -- the prior exact-match model implied only ~8.3% (wave 12's own row alone), which was the actual reported bug (simulating 12 waves completed only returned wave 12's loot, not the total across all waves cleared). Token (Varlamore) (wave 3 only, rarity=Varies) is excluded -- no fixed rate is stated anywhere on this page, and it is a cross-source token roll unrelated to the Colosseum's own mechanic, not part of the weighted-70 pool it sits beside (confirmed: wave 3's other 14 rows already sum exactly to 70 without it). 

WAVE-SCOPED DUPLICATE PROTECTION -- SHIPPED AS A WITH-REPLACEMENT APPROXIMATION, PER EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION, WITH THE SCOPE ITSELF UNRESOLVED AFTER TWO SEPARATE SESSIONS' WORTH OF CHECKING. The page's own citation ('Players are guaranteed to receive a full set prior to receiving duplicate Sunfire Fanatic pieces') does not state whether this resets each Colosseum attempt or is a permanent, account-wide guarantee. Checked directly, across two passes, none of which settled it: the Sunfire fanatic armour page; the individual Sunfire fanatic helm page; two web searches; an attempted fetch of the original Jagex 'First Look & Rewards' post (blocked, HTTP 403) and its OSRS Wiki mirror (Update:Fortis Colosseum - First Look & Rewards, fetched successfully -- discusses the armour's stats and design philosophy only, zero occurrences of 'duplicat'/'reset'/'attempt'/'account'); two further Jagex devblog mirrors from the same release cycle (Update:Poll Blog: Fortis Colosseum x Perilous Moons, Update:Varlamore: Part One - Reward Changes -- same result, zero relevant occurrences); the Rewards Chest and Fortis Colosseum pages' own full patch-history ==Changes== sections (no entry ever mentions this mechanic's scope, though OTHER Colosseum mechanics in the same changelog DO explicitly distinguish per-wave from per-run scope when it matters, e.g. 'Doom stacks are now removed at the end of a wave, rather than being permanent for a run' -- making the complete absence of similar language here mildly suggestive but not dispositive either way); and Fortis Colosseum/Strategies. Modelled here as ordinary weighted draws with NO duplicate avoidance at all (no ownershipGate), on the assumption (still unverified, inherited from an earlier research pass) that the protection is run-scoped -- if it turns out to be lifetime-scoped instead, an EXACT model via ownershipGate (identical to ToA's jewel pool) is directly available and should replace this approximation; do not assume the current shape is final without re-checking. Per explicit instruction: stopping the investigation here and keeping the approximation. 

Quantified cost of the approximation (computed this session, not assumed small): the individual per-piece expected drop rate (what the simulator's headline numbers show) is IDENTICAL under both models, by symmetry -- E[a specific piece, e.g. helm] is the same whether or not duplicate-avoidance is modelled. The divergence is entirely in JOINT/same-run statistics the simulator does not currently surface as a headline number: across a full 12-wave clear, P(at least one duplicate armour piece this run) is ~0.20% under this approximation vs ~0.00025% under true dedup (an ~800x relative overstatement of that specific joint event, though both are absolute-tiny), and P(a complete 3-piece set in one run) is understated by about 4.4x (0.0035% vs 0.0157%). A user reading the capped 1,000-kill log closely enough to notice 2 identical armour pieces in the same logged run would be seeing something the real game would essentially never produce -- the same class of residual as CoX's elite-clue/Olmlet co-occurrence artifact, smaller in frequency here.
